plain: To break a law or cut into someone's rights

webster.text: To break, as contracts; to violate, either positively by contravention, or negatively by non-fulfillment or neglect of performance.

more.text: To destroy or hinder; as, to infringe efficacy.

example.quote: Let no act be passed by any one legislature which may infringe on the rights and liberties of another.
example.cite: Thomas Jefferson, A Summary View of the Rights of British America, 1774
